candidate.answerReason: Multiplying the equations and using their sum gives p+1/p=2 for p=xyz>0. Thus (p-1)^2=0 and xyz=1; the positive triple (3/2,2/5,5/3) satisfies the original equations.

methods.label: Form an equation for the product
methods.explanation:
We only need the product, so let \(p=xyz>0\). Multiplying the three given equations is useful because the expansion contains both \(p\) and its reciprocal.

Choosing the ordinary term from all three factors gives \(xyz=p\), and choosing all three reciprocal terms gives \(1/p\). The other six terms are \(x,y,z,1/x,1/y,1/z\). Their sum is exactly the sum of the three original equations. Consequently,
\[
4\cdot1\cdot\frac73
=p+\frac1p+\left(4+1+\frac73\right).
\]
This simplifies to
\[
p+\frac1p=2.
\]
Since \(p>0\), multiplying by \(p\) is valid and gives
\[
p^2-2p+1=(p-1)^2=0.
\]
A real square is zero only when its base is zero, so \(p=1\).

The conditions are attainable: \((x,y,z)=(3/2,2/5,5/3)\) gives the three sums \(3/2+5/2=4\), \(2/5+3/5=1\), and \(5/3+2/3=7/3\). Therefore \(xyz=1\), choice B.
methods.levelReason: Uses distributive expansion, rational-expression arithmetic, and a perfect-square equation, all within school algebra.

methods.label: Express everything in terms of y
methods.explanation:
The first two equations let us express \(x\) and \(z\) in terms of \(y\), reducing the system to one equation. They give
\[
x=\frac{4y-1}{y},
\qquad
z=\frac1{1-y}.
\]
Positivity requires \(y>1/4\) from \(x>0\), and \(y<1\) from \(1/z=1-y>0\). Thus \(1/4<y<1\), so all the denominators used below are nonzero.

Substitute into \(z+1/x=7/3\):
\[
\frac1{1-y}+\frac{y}{4y-1}=\frac73.
\]
Multiplying by \(3(1-y)(4y-1)\) gives
\[
3(4y-1)+3y(1-y)=7(1-y)(4y-1).
\]
After expansion and collection of terms,
\[
25y^2-20y+4=(5y-2)^2=0.
\]
Therefore \(y=2/5\), which lies in the required interval. The formulas above then give \(x=3/2\) and \(z=5/3\). Checking the original equations gives \(3/2+5/2=4\), \(2/5+3/5=1\), and \(5/3+2/3=7/3\), so no extraneous solution has been introduced. Hence
\[
xyz=\frac32\cdot\frac25\cdot\frac53=1,
\]
choice B.
